A_hf_bf16.name: HF BF16
notes: Canonical H.1 systems contract: ~512 prompt tokens, 64 generated, use_cache=True.

B_hf_bnb_int8_h1b.name: HF bitsandbytes INT8 (original H.1B)
notes: H.1B preserved latency/quality are the original INT8 baseline, not an optimized path.
bitsandbytes INT8 saved memory but suffered backend-wide latency overhead (quantize→INT8 GEMM→dequant + outlier mixed precision).
Peak VRAM listed as 4.6 GB in H.1B summary; H.1 systems peak is 4709.3 MB (same order).

C_h4_fair_int8.name: H.4 fair INT8 rerun
notes: Fair rerun with MatMul8bitLt warning spam suppressed. H.4 runtime variants were REJECTED.
Do not call bitsandbytes INT8 optimized. Faster than H.1B mainly due to fair timing (no log I/O), not a new backend.

D_h5_triton_int8.name: H.5 Triton-patched INT8
D_h5_triton_int8.backend: huggingface + bitsandbytes INT8 + Triton fuse on 72 gate/up layers
notes: Triton improved one hot decode microkernel (M=1, 9728×2560, +29.5% isolated) but did not improve full-model generate() throughput.
Not a production win. Prefill Triton path was slower than cuBLASLt; 180 other INT8 linears remained bitsandbytes.

E_vllm_bf16.name: vLLM BF16
notes: Quality 0.938 is a 16-example smoke; not comparable to H.1 1000-example pass rate.

F_vllm_fp8_ref.name: vLLM FP8 reference
notes: FP8 is 8-bit floating-point serving, NOT bitsandbytes INT8 and NOT integer INT8.
Reference only until full production selection is decided later.
vLLM 0.28.0 does not load bitsandbytes INT8 checkpoints.

interpretation: bitsandbytes INT8 saved memory but suffered backend-wide latency overhead.
H.4 did not produce an optimized INT8 runtime; fair rerun is still the unmodified bitsandbytes path.
Triton improved one hot decode microkernel but did not improve full-model generate() throughput. Not a production win.
vLLM BF16 is the current low-latency serving baseline.
vLLM FP8 is an 8-bit floating-point serving reference only. FP8 is not INT8.
Cost assumes 100% GPU occupancy at the measured single-request rate; no queueing, batching, or concurrency.
production_implications: Do not ship bitsandbytes INT8 for latency-sensitive serving on this GPU: memory win, large E2E/throughput loss.
Do not ship the H.5 Triton patch: isolated kernel gain, worse generate() than H.4 fair INT8.
Prefer vLLM BF16 as the current serving baseline among measured options.
Keep FP8 as a memory-saving serving reference pending a later production selection (quality protocol still smoke-only).
Do not start concurrency/load testing as part of H.6.
verdict_reason: Comparison and cost matrix assembled from existing measured artifacts with the provided $0.74/hour rate. No new runs.
